description: alarms.v2 §2.5: `at`, the acknowledgement identity. Computed twice by two scripts of the text's drafter that share no code, kept out of the repository, and never blessed. `writes`: one identity's acts in order, under the deployment `epoch` in seconds, each with the owner's clock at the act in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (`clock_ms`) -> the `at` its record carries, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch as core §7.6's JSON reading has it, or null for none. A raise, an escalation and a resolve take a new at: the clock in whole seconds, or one second after the greatest at the owner knows it wrote for the identity where the clock's second is not later than it. A refresh keeps the at its record holds. While the clock reads no instant the epoch codes (before the epoch, or 2^32 s or more after it), and where the new at would have no code, the record carries none. `known`, where given, is an at the owner knows of from before the case: an adopted alarm's. `applies`: an acknowledgement's at (`acked_at`) and the alarm's present at (`at`), each in milliseconds or null -> whether the acknowledgement applies: while the alarm's at is at most the acknowledged one, and never with no at on either side. `moves`: an alarms.v1 document's `timestamp`, in milliseconds, adopted under the epoch -> the `at` of its record: the timestamp in whole seconds, or null where that instant has no code; and whether an acknowledgement made against that timestamp still applies.

writes.note: a raise, an escalation, a refresh and a resolve, minutes apart: at is the clock's second, kept at the refresh
a burst: four transitions within one second date the last three ahead of the clock
a burst that outruns the clock: the fifth transition, 2.5 s later, is still one second after the fourth
the clock steps back an hour: at still moves forward, a second at a time
a device with no real-time clock at boot reads 1970, before the catalog's epoch: no at. Once its clock is set, the next transition carries one
a clock that loses its code between two transitions: the at after the gap is later than the one before it, so an acknowledgement of the first never applies to the third
no catalog, so the epoch is 0, and 1970 has a code
an adopted alarm keeps its at, and its next transition is later than it though the clock is not
the epoch's last second: one more transition within it has no code, so no at

applies.note: escalated since: at moved, and the acknowledgement no longer applies
refreshed since: at kept, and it applies
an acknowledgement of a later at, made against a record the reader has since seen stepped back by another run: it applies
the alarm has no at: nothing applies, and it is told again
an acknowledgement with no at, made of a record that had none: it applies to nothing
an acknowledgement with no at and an alarm with one
an acknowledgement made against alarms.v1's timestamp, in milliseconds, of an alarm since adopted: its at is that timestamp's second

moves.note: a timestamp on a whole second
a timestamp with milliseconds: at is its second, not after it
a timestamp before the catalog's epoch has no code: no at, and the acknowledgement lapses
